summary.text: 第 is conventionally analyzed as 竹, the bamboo element, paired with 弟 as a plausible sound cue. Its central meaning is “sequence” or “order,” and it commonly precedes a numeral to mark an ordinal. The proposed link to bamboo writing strips is not confirmed by early-form evidence.

formation.text: The received form is best analyzed as phonosemantic: 竹 contributes a bamboo-related category, while 弟 plausibly cues the pronunciation. A competing dictionary label calls 第 pictographic, though its detailed analysis describes 竹 plus 弟. Historical accounts propose that 第 may once have been written 弟 alone or that 弟 was shortened in a common form; the timing and graphic change are unresolved. The proposed connection between bamboo and writing strips is not confirmed by early forms.

components.text: ⺮ is the bamboo radical side form, mapped to 竹. This identifies the visible component but does not establish a chronological change from 竹.

弟 plausibly supplies the sound cue in the received-form analysis. Accounts also propose that 第 was once written 弟 alone or that 弟 was shortened in a common form, but the timing and graphic change are unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: The readings support a plausible sound role but do not identify 弟’s earliest referent or recover its original spoken name.

sound.text: Zhengzhang gives matching Old Chinese forms for one reading of 弟.
In Baxter–Sagart, the forms share a sound base but differ in final and tone marking.

history.text: Historical-form indexes list oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, seal, and clerical categories, but do not explain individual forms. The proposal that 第 was once written 弟 remains undated; no sequence of graphic changes is established.

uncertainties.text: The bamboo-writing explanation is proposed rather than demonstrated by early forms. Accounts also differ: one describes 第 as pictographic, while others analyze it as 竹 plus 弟.
弟 is a plausible sound component, but its earliest referent and original name are not recovered. The proposed connection with 梯 and language-specific contraction accounts are uncorroborated here.

senses.text: Dictionary accounts give “sequence” or “order,” but the earliest attestation is unsettled: one quotation has 第，次也, while an inspected transcription has 弟，次也. The text’s composition date and witness history are unresolved.
第 commonly precedes a numeral to mark an ordinal. The first occurrence of this use is not dated here.

senses.period: Han text example; broader dating unresolved
senses.text: A Han text uses 第 for ranking performances. Dictionary accounts also record examination rank and evaluation; these uses do not establish the graph’s original meaning.
A text dated 815 uses 第 to refer to the time after passing an examination. How this use developed from sequence or rank is unresolved.
Dictionary accounts record a residence sense and offer a rank-related explanation, but its date and development are unresolved.
Dictionary accounts record an adverbial “only” or “just” sense. Its history and any relation to “sequence” are unresolved.

limitations.text: The links among sequence, ordinal marking, ranking, examination success, residence, and “only/just” are not established, so these senses are presented separately rather than as a semantic chain.
The earliest sequence attestation is unsettled: one dictionary quotation gives 第, while the inspected 小爾雅 transcription gives 弟. The text’s composition date and witness history are unresolved.

overview.text: 第 combines a bamboo-related element with 弟 as a plausible sound cue. It means “sequence” or “order” and commonly marks an ordinal before a numeral.

components.text: ⺮ is a bamboo radical side form mapped to 竹; the proposed writing-strip explanation is separate.
The matching modern readings make 弟 a plausible sound cue. Zhengzhang matches for one 弟 reading; Baxter–Sagart marks a final difference.

relationships.text: The received-form analysis assigns the bamboo side form a semantic role in 第.
Modern and reconstructed readings support 弟 as a plausible sound component in 第, though 弟’s earliest referent and name remain unrecovered.
